newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr pauses for breath after sell-off, ends flat.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr pauses for breath after sell-off, ends flat.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar paused for breath to close flat on Thursday after Wednesday's dizzy decline, but dealers said the downward trend was still in place.
"I think there's still a little bit more room to attack the downside," said one.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6600/07, up slightly on its 0.6595/00 open after a quiet day's trade. On its Trade-Weighted Index, the Kiwi was firmer at 65.60 from 65.47 at the open.
On Wednesday the Kiwi plunged over half a U.S. cent to set an 18-month low at 0.6578, but recovered 20 points by the close.

"I feel there were a few weak shorts out there that perhaps sold the break under 66 (U.S.) cents on the view that it was really going a lot lower," a dealer said of the Kiwi's sharp decline on Wednesday.
"They were disappointed so they turned around and stopped themselves out, but there's still interest to sell on rallies towards 0.6610."
Dealers said the Kiwi was likely to trade a 0.6580-6620 range until it got a shove from a move in another currency, particularly the Aussie or dollar/yen.

Data released this session showing a 4.6 percent fall in May retail sales, a 5.4 percent rise in registered unemployed in June, and a further decline in business confidence in the June quarter, had little impact on the currency, dealers said.
The data confirmed the economy was not "climbing out of its hole yet", said one, but that had been anticipated.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746 e-mail wellington.newsroom@reuters.com
